metadata.title: Daniel Dennett vs Dinesh D'Souza: Is God a Human Invention?
metadata.label: Religion, naturalism, and divine explanation
metadata.motion: Is God a human invention, or do cosmological fine-tuning, morality, consciousness, and religious experience provide rational support for a real divine creator?
metadata.sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 56cdc0474e9feebece154804df2a698dd092a212a6a29c073fc8059d80202de7). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
metadata.scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.

routes.description: Establish that religions and concepts of God are products of cultural evolution and human design, while showing that cosmology, apparent design, consciousness, morality, and social value admit naturalistic accounts that do not require a supernatural creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the human-development account explains religious concepts and the principal phenomena offered for theism can be understood without treating a divine creator as the necessary or preferable explanation.

motionBridge.description: Connect the historical and cultural evolution of God concepts to the conclusion that they are human constructions rather than discoveries of a real supernatural creator.

centralBridges.description: Provide bottom-up natural explanations for apparent design, consciousness, agency, and morality without presupposing a superior originating mind.
Show that cosmic beginnings and life-permitting conditions do not entail divine causation and that invoking a creator leaves substantial explanatory demands unresolved.
Ground moral development and social cooperation in human capacities, shared inquiry, and revisable institutions rather than continuing supernatural authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why publicly testable and self-correcting inquiry can examine religious, experiential, and consciousness claims without granting them automatic supernatural significance.
Account for religion's persistence and historical social contributions while distinguishing those functions from evidence that its supernatural claims are true.

routes.description: Establish that a real divine creator offers a unified explanation for the universe's beginning and order, life-permitting conditions, rational consciousness, free agency, morality, and religious experience, while showing that human formation of religious concepts does not imply an unreal referent.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the convergent cosmological, experiential, mental, and moral considerations provide rational support for divine reality and withstand the claim that cultural evolution or naturalistic explanation makes God merely a human invention.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative explanatory case from cosmos, mind, morality, and experience to rational support for a creator existing independently of human concepts.

centralBridges.description: Infer an explanatory ground beyond nature from the beginning, lawful order, and life-permitting structure of the universe.
Show that consciousness, rational understanding, intentional choice, and responsibility are not adequately exhausted by deterministic material processes.
Explain objective moral commitments, human dignity, and substantial altruism through a transcendent foundation that secular inheritance alone may not sustain.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend religious experience and other subjectively accessed realities as potentially rational evidence despite limits on direct public observation.
Distinguish the human development and disagreement of religious concepts from the separate question whether those concepts refer to an independent reality.

sections.title: Religious Concepts, Cultural Evolution, and Independent Reality
sections.rationale: This issue directly frames the motion: whether the development, variation, and human transmission of religions and God concepts establish invention, or remain compatible with reference to a reality independent of those concepts.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Natural Law, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: The universe's beginning, intelligible order, and life-permitting parameters form the principal cosmological case for a creator and the principal clash over anthropic, multiverse, regress, and explanatory alternatives.

sections.title: Consciousness, Reason, Free Will, and Evolutionary Explanation
sections.rationale: Whether consciousness, truth-directed reason, intentional choice, and responsibility can arise through natural processes or require a nonmaterial foundation is a major test of the rival explanatory frameworks.

sections.title: Morality, Human Dignity, and Secular Social Order
sections.rationale: The competing accounts of moral origins, normative authority, altruism, equality, and the durability of secular institutions bear directly on whether morality supplies rational support for God.

sections.title: Religious Experience, Cognitive Limits, and Epistemic Standards
sections.rationale: This issue determines what evidential status religious experience may have and whether public testing, subjective access, human cognitive limits, disagreement, and parsimony favor or exclude theistic belief.
